principles.title: Make the braking phase repeatable
principles.mechanism: Approach speed and available grip change the slowing demand.
principles.check: Compare braking onset, deceleration and release over repeated clean laps before testing a change.
principles.limitations: A brake-pedal percentage is not pressure, locking evidence or a universal target.

principles.title: Judge the exit through the next acceleration zone
principles.mechanism: An exit difference continues to affect the following straight.
principles.check: Compare sustained throttle pickup and section time through the following acceleration zone.
principles.limitations: Earlier throttle is a testable idea only when the measured exit improves.

principles.title: Review linked corners as one section
principles.mechanism: A line or speed choice can change the preparation for the next corner.
principles.check: Keep a change only if the linked section improves, even when one entry becomes slower.
principles.limitations: No line, apex position or corner identity is inferred without spatial evidence.

principles.title: Relate pedal transitions to steering demand
principles.mechanism: Turning and acceleration or braking draw on the same finite grip.
principles.check: Inspect brake release and throttle pickup alongside steering and speed at the same track position.
principles.limitations: More trail braking, less coasting or more throttle is not always the answer.

principles.title: Check balance through load transitions
principles.mechanism: Crests, compressions and direction changes can alter the load supported by the tyres.
principles.check: Use repeatable speed and input traces to locate the phase of instability before a setup experiment.
principles.limitations: No damper, ride-height or spring value can be prescribed from a category or circuit name.

principles.title: Check tyre trends against this stint
principles.mechanism: Repeated sliding and loading may change tyre behaviour during a run.
principles.check: Compare available temperatures, pressures and pace trends at similar fuel and track conditions.
principles.limitations: No real-world tyre pressure or temperature limit is transferred to an unknown AC compound.

principles.title: Recheck the baseline when conditions change
principles.mechanism: A changing surface or tyre state can change the value of an old comparison.
principles.check: Compare fresh clean laps under similar grip and tyre conditions before moving a braking landmark.
principles.limitations: Real-weather descriptions do not prove the simulated surface is wet, hot or dusty.

principles.title: Confirm the car systems before coaching them
principles.mechanism: Assists and energy systems vary between cars, eras and mods.
principles.check: Use reported ABS, TC and energy capabilities and valid channels; otherwise describe them as unavailable.
principles.limitations: GT3 or Formula labels alone do not establish ABS, TC, ERS, DRS or their setting scales.

principles.title: Separate energy strategy from driving error
principles.mechanism: Supported hybrid deployment can change acceleration despite similar pedal inputs.
principles.check: Compare state of charge and deployment only when exposed and valid; otherwise withhold energy optimisation claims.
principles.limitations: A non-hybrid Formula car and a prototype without exposed energy telemetry cannot receive an ERS prescription.

principles.title: Keep legacy GT2/GTE separate from modern SRO GT2
principles.mechanism: The same GT2 label has been used by different generations of racing classes.
principles.check: Compare only the exact car and known specification; keep class-based braking and traction claims conditional.
principles.limitations: Modern SRO GT2 performance descriptions must not be applied to AC BMW M3 GT2 or Ferrari 458 GT2.

principles.title: Use the road-car baseline and actual tyre compound
principles.mechanism: Road-car tyres, assistance and setup choices differ from dedicated race cars.
principles.check: Build a repeatable baseline with the actual compound and reported assists before comparing a race-car technique.
principles.limitations: A road-going 911 GT3 RS is not a homologated GT3 race car.

categories.name: GT3
limits: BoP, electronics scales and tyre windows are car/version specific.

categories.name: Formula / single-seater
limits: Formula includes very different eras and levels; no universal aero, gear or hybrid assumption is made.

categories.name: Legacy GT2 / GTE
limits: Legacy GT2/GTE is not modern SRO GT2. Confirm each car system from telemetry.

categories.name: Modern SRO GT2
limits: Higher-power/lower-aero real-world class context is not a physics assertion about an arbitrary AC mod.

categories.name: GT4
limits: Road-derived category context; exact homologation, BoP and electronics remain unverified.

categories.name: Prototype / sports racer
limits: Prototype covers hybrid LMP1 and non-hybrid historical cars; do not generalise one model to all.

categories.name: Road car
limits: Actual road tyre and driver assists take precedence over racing class names.

categories.name: Historic single-seater
limits: Historical tyre, gearbox and assist behaviour must be confirmed for the exact simulation.

rules.text: Lead with one actionable next step, then one measured reason. Longer explanation belongs in the debrief.
Schedule nonurgent coaching on a straight or other verified low-workload phase; suppress it during braking, heavy steering and close battles.
Filter competing messages into one priority. Do not recite every available measurement.
Respect quiet mode and answer explicit requests; urgent valid car-health warnings may take priority.
State what was measured and keep uncertainty explicit; avoid confident fault labels from one scalar difference.
